The dream: how it runs, what a skill receives, what it may write

DreamWorkflow (DESIGN §7) runs on the devbox's local Temporal (127.0.0.1:7233, namespace brain) inside brain-worker. The hourly Schedule brain-dream-hourly starts DreamTickWorkflow, which runs the dream as a child named dream/<UTC hour>; brain dream run --now [--shadow] starts one directly under the same id.

gate ─► snapshot ─► reconcile ─► capture ─► learn ─► demote ─► file ─► curate.link ─► curate.hubs ─► curate.merge ─► curate.cards ─► summarise ─► render ─► check ─► verify ─► reindex ─► commit
det      git+tar     det          brain CLI   distil   det        file    link           hubs        merge             card            summarise    brain CLI  lint      verify    brain CLI   state+report+git
                                              Opus     (index)    Haiku   Opus           Opus        Opus ×≤2          Haiku ×≤4       Haiku                   (revert)  Opus

demote sets node_stats.demoted_at on a node shown 10 times as a pointer and never opened or followed, and clears it when the node is opened (rank.Demote). It is a ranking prior: it changes no file and no status.

Gate

Material = .md files changed after the area's watermark in .brain/dream-state.json:

Area Roots Per-run cap Consumed by
sessions sessions/ 60 learn (distil)
captures memory/ (not MEMORY.md), inbox/ — the one-time .import/ copies are filed by brain file, not the dream 40 file (file)
docs work/, plus the shadow root (saahil-docs, read-only) presented as work/… with --shadow 10 big docs (≥ 20 KB) summarise (summarise)

Oldest first; what is over the cap waits. A watermark advances only when its step ran (an ok answer, cached or not, or no input) — a missing skill, a cost stop or a failure leaves the material for the next dream. Before the first dream the docs area starts 24 h back; older docs are the backfill's job. notes/, hubs/, journal/ and work/<box>/CARD.md are never scanned, so the dream's own writes do not wake the next dream.

Skip when nothing is new; otherwise run only if ≥ 12 h since the last dream or ≥ 30 new sessions (--now lifts this rule only). Lock: .brain/dream.lock (pid, start, run id), stale after 3 h.

LLM steps — the skill contract

The skill is <repo>/skills/<name>.md (brain-worker --skills); a missing file is a recorded skip. It is passed as --append-system-prompt to claude --bare -p --model <m> --output-format json --max-budget-usd <x> --no-session-persistence --json-schema <EditsSchema>, in an empty working directory, with this JSON on stdin:

{"step": "file",
 "material": [{"path": "memory/feedback-x.md", "content": "…", "truncated": false}],
 "proposed": [{"path": "notes/finding-y.md", "action": "write", "content": "…", "why": "…"}],
 "files_left_out": 0}

material is the area's files (≤ 16 KB each, ≤ 400 KB in all); proposed is every edit earlier steps of this run asked for (curate.link, curate.hubs and verify read only this). The answer must match EditsSchema (edits.go):

{"edits": [{"path": "notes/finding-y.md", "action": "write", "content": "<whole file>", "why": "…"}], "notes": "…"}

Applied only when: action is write; the path is a clean relative .md path under notes/ hubs/ journal/ memory/ work/ or is hot.md / index.md; no dot-folder; no symlinked file; the real directory is inside the brain root and not under saahil-docs or ~/.claude; content ≤ 64 KB; the step's share of the 50-edit cap is not full (learn and file get what is left; curate.link, curate.hubs, curate.merge, curate.cards and verify each get an equal share of what is left with the curation steps after them, so the first cannot starve the rest; an edit over the share is held). Anything else is listed in the report's rejected; a delete is never applied and is counted in deletions_rejected. Identical content is a no-op, not an edit. Every overwritten file is first copied to .archive/dream/<run-id>/before/.

A delta skill's answer is applied in dry run first. An op the applier refuses there (a cap, an id that does not resolve) becomes no edit: the step record counts it in refused, and its reason names the first one.

curate.merge — merge, do not copy

Filing makes about one note per memory. Thus one rule can exist as several global notes, and an old rule can contradict a newer one. curate.merge finds these notes and changes them with checked deltas. It never deletes.

Part What it does
gate (MergeGate) Reads every current global note: id, type, as_of, project (from a .import/<machine>/<repo>/ source), summary. Runs when this list is not the list that the last complete merge left (.brain/merge-state.json), or 24 h after that merge. With no change, the same input gets a $0 answer from the ledger.
find (MergeStep, Opus) The merge skill, stage find, names duplicate groups, conflicts (supersede, narrow or owner) and stale notes.
settle (code) Keeps only ids of current global notes, each in one group. Keeps the newest note of a group. Sends a supersede or narrow between equal or missing dates to the owner. Replaces a stale note only with a note of the same or a later date. A note that the plan supersedes takes no further part. At most 20 groups per run.
bodies (MergeStep, Opus) Stage bodies, one call for each group, writes the body of the kept note. The body holds every distinct fact of the group, within the cap of the type. A failed call costs only its group, and the ledger keeps each answer on the notes of its group.
units (code) Group: update_note (replace_body) and one supersede for each other note. Narrow: append "Narrowed by : " and a related link; not again when the line is there. Conflict supersede and stale: supersede. Owner: a question, no edit. The applier checks the units in dry run. When it refuses one op of a unit, the step drops the full unit.
apply ApplyEdits, as for every step: backups, the 50-edit cap, revert when lint fails.
done (MergeDone) Appends the new owner pairs to .brain/owner-questions.jsonl (ids, as_of, question, created; one line for each pair, never two). Writes the list as the merge left it, so the writes of the merge do not start the next merge.

The coordinator relays the owner questions. It sets answered on a line when it applies the answer of the owner. brain doctor shows how many questions wait: not answered, and both notes still current.

When the bodies call of a group does not run or gives no usable body (cost cap, failure), that group waits. The other groups, the conflicts and the stale notes still apply. A waiting group is found again by the merge of the next day, so a group that fails each time costs at most one try a day. The manual sweep of 2026-10-08 paid $0.78 for the find (248 notes) and $0.67 for the bodies of 15 groups in one call; a dry run at 23:25Z paid $0.91 for the find (267 notes), and one call for 15 groups went over a $1 budget, which is why each group now has its own call.

brain dream merge is a dry run against the brain: it shows the gate, the plan after the checks of the code, each file that would change, and the owner questions. It applies nothing, queues nothing, and keeps its ledger outside the brain (--ledger <dir>, else a temp folder). --budget (per call, default $1) and --cap (default $2) limit it; --out <file> writes the delta for brain apply-delta. --find-answer uses a recorded find answer instead of a model call; the bodies calls then go to the model, unless --bodies-answer gives a recorded answer for them too.

curate.cards — a CARD follows its box

The start digest gives the CARD of a box to each session in that box. The backfill wrote the CARDs once; this step keeps them current. On 2026-10-09 the image-lane CARD (22:28Z) said "nothing merged", while its STATE (00:25Z) had 10 merged PRs.

Part What it does
plan (CardsPlan) Live brain only (in shadow the step is skipped). For each box in work/: the newest regular file outside bulk folders (artifacts/, cache*, venv/, dot-folders; CARD.md is not work) and the mtime of CARD.md. A box is stale when that file is ≥ 1 h newer than its CARD, or when it has files and no CARD. A done or paused CARD is no exception: new work after it (a resumed campaign) makes it stale, and with no new work it stays. Stalest first: no CARD, then the longest lag. At most 4 boxes for each dream; the others wait. Nothing stale: skipped, no stale cards.
refresh (BackfillCard, Haiku) The card skill on the box inventory, as in the backfill, one box at a time. The call is keyed to the dream (curate.cards/<box>) and paid under the $8 cap of the run, with the spend of the run before it. A refused answer is asked again once.
apply The CARD comes back as an edit for ApplyEdits: backup, lint, revert, the 50-edit cap. CARDs do not go to verify, which checks notes. An answer equal to the CARD on disk only touches its mtime, so the box is not picked again until its work changes.
record refreshed, unchanged (touched), skipped (with the reason, for example the cost cap), failed and wait for the next dream, with box names only (≤ 10 for each list).

When the cap stops a call, the step skips the boxes that are left, with the reason, and the later LLM steps of the run stop too. brain dream cards --dry-run shows what the plan would pick now: each stale box with the age and status of its CARD and its newest file. It reads only; it calls no model and writes nothing.

Cost and idempotency

Key = sha256(workflow, step, model, sha(skill), sha(input)) in llm_calls (.index/brain.db); a done key is answered from .data/llm/<key>.json for $0, so a retry or rerun never pays twice. Before a paid call: run spent + step budget (Opus $2.50, Haiku $0.50) must be ≤ $8, and today's spend (UTC, failed attempts included)

  • step budget ≤ $100 (owner, 2026-10-08: up to $1,000 is fine; the $8 per-run cap stays); otherwise no more LLM calls this run, with the reason recorded, and the deterministic steps finish. The prompt text is never stored or logged — only its hash.

Failure modes

Call Timeout Retries On final failure
deterministic activities (gate, snapshot, apply, git, brain CLI) 15 min 3, 5 s backoff ×2 gate/snapshot/commit: run fails, state not advanced, report written; others: step recorded failed, run goes on
LLM step 20 min 2, 30 s backoff (a crash after the model answered can pay again) step failed; a model-side error (budget hit, error result) is not retried and its cost is counted
brain lint exit ≥ 2 — — every file this run edited is restored from .archive/dream/<run-id>/before/; files it created move to …/reverted/

Never deletes: reverts and the lock file are the only removals, and reverts move files into the archive.

Operating

systemctl --user status brain-temporal brain-worker        # deploy/systemd/*.service, user units
brain dream status                                          # last runs, next tick, cost today
brain dream schedule [--shadow=false]                       # create/update brain-dream-hourly
temporal schedule toggle --schedule-id brain-dream-hourly --unpause --reason go -n brain --address 127.0.0.1:7233
brain-worker --llm fake                                     # no model: empty edits (shadow checks)
brain dream merge [--ledger <dir>] [--out delta.json]          # what curate.merge would change; applies nothing
brain dream cards --dry-run                                 # the stale CARDs curate.cards would refresh now

Reports: .brain/dream-runs/<run-id>.json per run; the latest skip in .brain/dream-last-skip.json. The replay fixture testdata/dream-history.json comes from a run against a synthetic brain; re-record it (run, then temporal workflow show -w dream/<hour> -n brain --output json) when the workflow's step order changes on purpose. It is from before curate.merge and must replay without the step. testdata/dream-merge-history.json goes through a merge that edits notes (from before curate.cards); testdata/dream-cards-history.json goes through a CARD refresh. go test -tags record -run 'TestRecord(Merge|Cards)History' ./internal/dream records them again on a throwaway dev server.
